title: Smokey and the Bandit
tagline: A truck full of beer. Pass the ribs.
about: A bootlegger runs a truckload of beer across state lines with a sheriff chasing him the whole way.
cue: Serve the mains when the Bandit picks up Frog by the side of the road.
faces: Showtime: Serve the mains when the Bandit picks up Frog by the side of the road.

    SnacksGeorgia boiled peanutsRaw peanuts simmered in salty Cajun water, served warm in paper cupsHow to make it500g raw peanuts in the shell80g fine salt1 tbsp Cajun seasoning2 L waterRinse the peanuts well and put them in a large pot with the water, salt and Cajun seasoning.Simmer with the lid on, topping up with water as needed, until the peanuts are soft.Turn off the heat and let the peanuts soak in the brine.Drain and serve warm in paper cups.Sheriff Justice's pickled okraGarlic and dill pickled okra with chilli, served cold with sharp cheddarHow to make it400g okra3 garlic cloves1 bunch dill1 red chilli300ml white vinegar200ml water1 tbsp salt200g vintage cheddarPack the okra into a clean jar with the garlic, dill and chilli.Boil the vinegar, water and salt together and pour over while hot.Cool, lid and pickle in the fridge for a week.Serve cold with the cheddar cut into chunks.Fred's cayenne pork cracklingCayenne crackling, split with FredHow to make itNot on tonight's cookPork rind dried overnight then roasted until puffed and crackling, broken into shards and dusted with smoked paprika, cayenne and salt, with a ranch dip.Score 600g pork rind in strips, rub well with salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Pat dry, lay skin up on a rack and roast at 240°C for 30 to 40 minutes until fully puffed and crackling.Break into shards and dust with 1 tsp smoked paprika, half a tsp cayenne and salt.Mix 150g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayo, garlic powder, dill and chives for dip.Runaway bride fried pickle spearsBreaker one-nine, Bandit needs a snack.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.GrillTruck stop chicken fried steakCrisp breaded steak under creamy black pepper gravyHow to make it4 minute steaks250g plain flour1 tsp salt200ml buttermilk400ml full cream milk2 tbsp plain flour for the gravy1 jar black peppercorns1kg potatoes60g butter250ml vegetable oilPeel and boil the potatoes until soft, then mash with the butter and some of the milk. Keep warm.Pound the steaks thin and season the flour with the salt and plenty of cracked black peppercorns.Dredge each steak in flour, then buttermilk, then flour again.Shallow fry in hot oil until deep golden and crisp, then keep warm on a rack.Whisk the gravy flour into the pan fat, add the remaining milk and lots of cracked pepper and simmer until thick.Serve the steaks over the mash with the gravy.28 hour Texarkana barbecue ribsPork rubbed with paprika and cayenne, tangy vinegar glaze, coleslaw, 400 cases of beer to haulHow to make itNot on tonight's cookPork ribs rubbed with paprika, brown sugar and cayenne, baked low and slow, glazed with a tangy vinegar barbecue sauce and charred, with crunchy coleslaw.Mix 2 tbsp paprika, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp cayenne and 2 tsp salt and rub over 2kg pork ribs.Wrap in foil and bake at 150°C for 2.5 hours.Simmer 125ml cider vinegar, 125ml tomato sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp chilli flakes for 5 minutes.Brush on the ribs and grill hot for 5 minutes.Toss half a shredded cabbage and a grated carrot with 125g mayo and vinegar.SweetsDouble or nothing peach cobblerCinnamon peaches under a soft biscuit topping, with vanilla ice creamHow to make it6 peaches80g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon1 lemon80g cold butter200g self-raising flour150ml full cream milk1 L vanilla ice creamHeat the oven to 190°C. Slice the peaches and toss with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a baking dish.Rub the butter into the flour, then stir in the milk to a thick batter.Drop spoonfuls of batter over the fruit and bake until golden and bubbling.Serve warm with scoops of ice cream.DrinksBandit's bourbon peach sweet teaSweet black tea with peaches and a shot of bourbon over iceHow to make it5 black tea bags1 L boiling water2 peaches100g caster sugar120ml bourbon1 lemon1 bunch mint1 bag iceSteep the tea bags in the boiling water with the sliced peaches and sugar for 6 minutes, then remove the bags.Chill the tea with the peaches in it until very cold.Fill four tall glasses with ice and add bourbon to each.Top with tea and finish with a squeeze of lemon, a peach slice and a sprig of mint.Ice cold Coors BanquetFour hundred cases, Texarkana to Atlanta, 28 hours.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
